annotations.title: Screen a Name Against Sanctions Lists

description:
Screen a name against the UK (OFSI), US (OFAC), EU and UN consolidated sanctions lists.

Returns every list entry whose primary name or alias matches, with the
regime, source reference and listing date where the source gives one. Use it to check whether a
counterparty — or its officers / persons with significant control —
appears on a sanctions list.

MATCHING is deterministic: normalised exact + alias match (case-, accent-
and punctuation-insensitive). A company/entity legal name matches reliably;
PERSON names with transliteration variants may not (e.g. 'Mohammed' vs
'Muhamad'). An empty result is therefore NOT a guarantee of clearance, and a
hit on a common name may be a false positive to disambiguate. This is a
screening aid, not a compliance determination.

`lists_screened` reports which of OFSI/OFAC/EU/UN were screened;
`lists_unavailable` names those that were not. Each list is refreshed on
its own: if a list's latest refresh failed, its previous load is still
screened and the list is named in `lists_stale`, for up to 7 days after
its last successful load (after that it is dropped and reported
unavailable). `list_as_at` gives each screened list's own load time, and
`as_at` is the oldest of them. `is_partial` is true whenever a list is
unavailable or stale, or a screened list is 24 hours old or more. When
`is_partial` is true an empty `hits` is UNRESOLVED, not clearance. If no
list has ever loaded the call raises a retryable error rather than
returning an empty screen.

entity_type.description: Optional filter: 'person' or 'entity' (a company is an 'entity'). Any other value is rejected. Omit to screen both.

name.description: Person or company/entity name to screen against the consolidated sanctions lists.

name: sanctions_screen

outputSchema.description: Result of screening one name against the consolidated sanctions lists.

as_at.description: The oldest load time among the screened lists (ISO 8601 UTC; see list_as_at), or null when no list was screened. Provenance for the screen — the lists update on designation.

entity_type_filter.description: entity_type filter applied to the screen ('person'/'entity'), or null.

hits.description: Matching list entries. An empty list means no exact/alias match on the screened lists — NOT a guarantee of clearance (see the tool description on matching limits).

items.description: A single sanctions-list entry matching a screened name.

entity_type.description: 'person' or 'entity' where the source distinguishes it; otherwise null.

is_alias.description: True if the match was on an alias/AKA rather than the primary listed name.

listed_on.description: Date the entity was listed, where the source provides it (ISO YYYY-MM-DD).

matched_name.description: The exact name or alias on the list that matched the query.

reference.description: The source's own reference for the listing (FCDO Unique ID, OFAC uid, EU reference number, or UN reference number).

regime.description: Sanctions programme/regime the listing falls under (e.g. 'Russia', 'CUBA', 'DRC').

is_partial.description: True when any expected list was unavailable or stale, or any screened list was loaded 24 hours ago or more (see list_as_at). When true, an empty hits list must be treated as UNRESOLVED, not as clearance.

list_as_at.description: Each screened list's own last successful load time on this server (ISO 8601 UTC), keyed by list name.

lists_screened.description: Which consolidated lists were screened for this call: each from its latest successful load, which may be a previous load if the latest refresh of that list failed (see lists_stale). A list absent here was NOT screened — see lists_unavailable. A list that fails part-way through a load contributes none of that load's entries.

lists_stale.description: Screened lists served from a previous load because the latest refresh of that list failed (kept for up to 7 days after its last successful load). Their entries were screened, but designations made since list_as_at for that list would not appear in hits.

lists_unavailable.description: Expected lists that have no usable load — never loaded, loaded to zero records, or last loaded more than 7 days ago — and so were NOT screened. Non-empty means this screen is incomplete: a name on one of these lists would not appear in hits. Absence of evidence here is not evidence of absence.

match_count.description: Number of list entries that matched the query.

normalized_query.description: The normalised form used for matching (upper-cased, accent- and punctuation-stripped, whitespace-collapsed).
